paper.title: GORDON: Graph-based Object-centric Rewards for Decomposition of Long-Horizon Manipulation
paper.source_version: arXiv v1, submitted 2026-08-04 14:43:41 UTC; versioned PDF SHA-256 2b068c624a58db12eae36bc71d54709395df888ad56ced794eacafe9a93a0725; TeX archive SHA-256 4b63c782d88322613a2a808b43f55d409ab14b7a2aad0da2affc179623f92839; official project page pinned at c617d3678f88a7ded57304eb804cfa47eaf51c65

decision_relevance.why_admitted: It supplies an executable object-centric reward form and a reward-trace-to-ordered-stage mechanism, while its separate subpolicies, stage-specific initialization, and motion planner make the fixed-trainer boundary explicit.
not_evidence_for: An implemented RL-Sculptor reward or oracle
Robot reference-motion composition or a policy-conditioning clock
A fixed-trainer causal effect of reward decomposition alone
Raw-video object detection or real-world perception reliability
Branching, recovery, predicate-conditioned, preference-conditioned, or learned-oracle execution
Equal total training compute across single-policy and multi-subpolicy methods
A reproducible public implementation at the pinned official-project commit

mechanisms.name: Object-centric scene-graph representation
mechanisms.description: Each video frame is converted to a fully connected graph whose nodes carry semantic class and 2D or 3D bounding-box geometry and whose edges encode pairwise spatial distance between boxes.

mechanisms.name: Persistent activity weighting with robot masking
mechanisms.description: Scale-normalized box-center displacement marks active objects, active non-robot nodes receive higher pooling weight, activity persists after first activation, and robot nodes are removed before message passing and pooling.

mechanisms.name: Temporally aligned reconstructive graph embedding
mechanisms.description: A GraphTransformer, weighted pooling operator, and projection head are trained with temporal cycle consistency plus class and bounding-box reconstruction, then frozen for policy optimization.

mechanisms.name: Goal-distance reward with classifier-gated terminal bonus
mechanisms.description: The dense term is negative Euclidean distance from the current graph embedding to the mean final-frame embedding; a goal classifier trained on the last portion of demonstrations adds a thresholded terminal bonus.

mechanisms.name: Reward-gradient stage discovery and local reward learning
mechanisms.description: After temporal normalization, significant changes in the full-task reward gradient define an ordered segmentation; each segment supplies demonstrations for a separately trained encoder, local goal, and local reward.

mechanisms.name: Sequential specialized-subpolicy executor
mechanisms.description: One policy is optimized for each discovered stage; deployment switches on detected stage completion, while training perturbs stage starts and a collision-aware planner repositions the arm between stages.

failure_modes.name: Final-goal distance loses internal stage guidance
failure_modes.description: States can be close to the final embedding without satisfying semantic completion; in long-horizon tasks, full-task environmental and learned baselines make partial progress but fail later stages and score zero full-task success.

failure_modes.name: Dense reward is insufficient for contact-rich completion
failure_modes.description: On PutShoesInBox, the learned distance reward without a terminal bonus solves opening only, scores 2.5% on first-shoe placement, 0% on second-shoe placement, and 0% after composition.

failure_modes.name: Privileged object-annotation dependence
failure_modes.description: All experiments construct reward graphs from simulator-provided boxes, semantic classes, and robot labels; moderate synthetic noise does not validate a detector or raw-video deployment pipeline.

failure_modes.name: Under-specified stage boundary and switch logic
failure_modes.description: The paper gives no numerical reward-gradient threshold, temporal normalization/alignment details, smoothing rule, or per-task classifier thresholds, and it does not fully specify how detected completion drives switching.

failure_modes.name: Reward decomposition is bundled with trainer-side interventions
failure_modes.description: Long-horizon GORDON jointly changes reward models, policy count, stage initial-state distributions, switching, and inter-stage motion planning; the paper does not normalize total compute across the resulting number of subpolicies.

failure_modes.name: Simulation-only and partially unmatched evaluation
failure_modes.description: Results use five seeds and 16 simulator episodes per seed, some task standard deviations are large, and RoboHorizon is a semantically matched published-result comparison without rollouts for identical cumulative predicates.

failure_modes.name: Reward discrimination is not an independent objective metric
failure_modes.description: The paper's rho diagnostic is a ratio of cumulative returns produced by the learned reward itself; it can inspect reward separation but cannot replace simulator-predicate task success in Sam's evaluator.

failure_modes.name: No public implementation at the pinned version
failure_modes.description: The official project repository contains the project page and media but marks code as coming soon, so algorithmic details and reported settings cannot be checked against executable source.

evaluation.name: Seven-task SAC policy evaluation
evaluation.description: Three short-horizon and four long-horizon simulation tasks use common reported policy architecture, action space, and training budget, with success averaged over five seeds and 16 simulator-predicate episodes per seed.

evaluation.name: Full-task and cumulative stage success
evaluation.description: Table I reports 74.4% mean GORDON full-task success across four long-horizon tasks; Table II reports ordered cumulative and conditional stage success to expose where sequences fail.

evaluation.name: Reward-profile boundary alignment
evaluation.description: Figure 6 visually compares inferred reward-profile boundaries against simulator-annotated stage endings for three representative long-horizon tasks; no numeric boundary metric is reported.

evaluation.name: Appearance and localization reward-discrimination stress test
evaluation.description: PutShoesInBox reward discrimination compares raw-pixel, object-centric, robot-included, and robot-masked models under color shifts and synthetic bounding-box noise.

evaluation.name: Terminal-bonus and subtask-transfer ablation
evaluation.description: PutShoesInBox compares environmental bonus only, environmental reward, learned reward without bonus, learned reward with environmental bonus, and learned reward with its classifier bonus for individual and composed policies.

evaluation.name: TCC and reconstruction objective ablation
evaluation.description: Holding encoder, pooling, and validation split fixed, the combined objective yields rho 0.629 versus 0.798 for TCC only and 0.837 for reconstruction only.

evaluation.name: One-task RLBench-to-ManiSkill3 correspondence diagnostic
evaluation.description: TakeUmbrellaOut reaches 100% in both simulators; the paper reports lower steps and wall time for ManiSkill3, including a 32-environment parallel run, but tests only one task.

evidence.locator: arXiv metadata and submission history; v1 submitted 2026-08-04 14:43:41 UTC
evidence.claim: The pinned public source is arXiv:2608.03753v1, a 2026 cs.RO preprint by Andrea Protopapa, Davide Buoso, Francesca Pistilli, Georgia Chalvatzaki, and Giuseppe Averta.
Frames are represented as fully connected object graphs with semantic class and 2D/3D bounding-box node descriptors and pairwise box-distance edges.

evidence.locator: Section III-A, Equations 1-3 and Weighted Graph Pooling paragraphs
evidence.claim: Pooling upweights active objects, activity uses normalized center displacement and persists, and robot nodes are zeroed, disconnected, and assigned zero pooling weight.
The graph encoder combines temporal cycle consistency with bounding-box, centroid, generalized-IoU, and object-class reconstruction.
The reward is negative L2 distance to an averaged final-frame goal embedding plus a classifier bonus thresholded by a validation-selected goal probability.

evidence.locator: Section III-C, Subtasks discovery and Subtask reward and policy learning
evidence.claim: Significant changes in temporally normalized full-task reward gradients determine ordered segments, and each segment receives a separately trained encoder and local reward.

evidence.locator: Section III-C, Subpolicy training and composition
evidence.claim: The method trains one policy per stage, switches on detected completion, perturbs each subpolicy's initial states, and uses collision-aware planning to reposition between stages.

evidence.locator: Section IV, setup paragraphs before Section IV-A
evidence.claim: The seven-task simulation study uses 100 MAGICAL and 25 per-task ManiSkill3 demonstrations, simulator object annotations, alpha 2.0, k 40, tau 0.005, lambda_rec 0.5, beta 5, lambda_box 0.9, lambda_giou 0.1, lambda_cls 1.0, q 3%, and frozen GraphTransformer encoders during policy optimization.

evidence.locator: Section IV, baselines and evaluation protocol paragraphs
evidence.claim: Policies use SAC with the same reported architecture, action space, and training budget; results use five seeds and 16 episodes per seed, while RoboHorizon is a semantically matched published-result comparison without rollout-level predicates.

evidence.locator: Table I and Section IV-A Policy Evaluation Across Tasks
evidence.claim: GORDON reports 74.4% average long-horizon success, 25.4 percentage points above decomposed environmental reward and 35.3 points above RoboHorizon; the full-task environmental, XIRL, and GraphIRL policies report zero full-task average.

evidence.locator: Figure 6 and Section IV-A Learned Reward Profiles
evidence.claim: Inferred reward-profile boundaries visually align with simulator stage endings for three representative long-horizon tasks; the paper reports no numeric boundary-detection metric.

evidence.locator: Section IV-B Reward Discrimination and Table III
evidence.claim: The diagnostic is the ratio of learned cumulative returns on successful and unsuccessful trajectories; with 1 cm center and 5% half-extent Gaussian noise per axis, the robot-masked variant reports rho 0.583 and remains at rho 0.629 under the color shift.

evidence.locator: Section IV-B Subtask-Level Reward Transfer and Table IV
evidence.claim: On PutShoesInBox, learned reward without bonus has 0% composed success, while the learned classifier bonus produces 81.5% mean composed success with 12.0% standard deviation.

evidence.locator: Section IV-B Training Objective Ablation and Table V
evidence.claim: Reward-discrimination rho is 0.798 for TCC only, 0.837 for reconstruction only, and 0.629 for both objectives.
TakeUmbrellaOut reaches 100% in both simulators; RLBench uses 900000 steps and 474 minutes, ManiSkill3 serial uses 150000 steps and 57 minutes, and 32-way ManiSkill3 uses 50000 steps and 27 minutes.

evidence.locator: Section V, second and third paragraphs
evidence.claim: The authors state that a single full-task reward is generally insufficient in long-horizon tasks and that early-stage success can collapse on later cumulative stages.

evidence.locator: Official project repository, commit c617d3678f88a7ded57304eb804cfa47eaf51c65, docs/js/project-data.js lines 28-31
evidence.claim: The pinned official project page links the paper and marks code as coming soon rather than providing an implementation repository.

evidence.locator: Table II and Section IV-A Policy Evaluation Across Tasks
evidence.claim: Ordered cumulative and conditional success rates show that full-task environmental, XIRL, and GraphIRL policies sometimes complete initial stages but fall to zero on later cumulative stages.
